transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um... I guess I'm here because I'm having some trouble with my work. I'm a teacher, so I have a lot of grading and planning. 

But I'll sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, you know, fully intending to just get it done. And then... maybe ten minutes go by, and I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same page. My mind will be on two or three completely different things, and I'm barely taking in what's right in front of me. So... yeah. I guess that's why I'm here.
Does this difficulty with staying on task happen in other areas of your life, like during hobbies, social conversations, or household chores, or is it strictly limited to your work?

Yeah, um... I suppose it happens other times too. Like... in planning meetings. Or just at home with my wife. 

I'll be looking right at them, you know, nodding along... but then they'll ask what I think, and... I realize I've completely missed the actual point of what they just said. So... yeah. It's not just the paperwork.
Looking back at your time in grade school, did you struggle with these same issues of staying focused and drifting off during lessons?

Yeah... I guess so. Um... even back in primary school, my report cards would usually say things like... "bright but careless." Or that I wouldn't finish my work unless I was being closely supervised. 

And... my parents were always finding these old worksheets just crumpled up at the bottom of my backpack. Things I had completely forgotten to turn in. So... yeah. I guess it's been happening for a while.
